key_insight: HA-DSB translates PET-guided whole-body MRI by adapting diffusion transport to different anatomical regions and lesion heterogeneity.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help shorten PET-MR workflows by generating higher-quality MRI with better lesion detail across the whole body.
method: Models MRI translation as a stochastic diffusion Schrödinger bridge between source and target image distributions.
Uses vision-language model region embeddings to make the translation region-specific across heterogeneous anatomy.
Injects PET-derived metabolic priors in both forward noise modulation and reverse attention to emphasize lesion-relevant structures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments showing superior whole-body translation performance across body regions and improved lesion-area quality under PET guidance.
watch_item: Performance may depend on reliable region labels, PET availability, and careful validation before use in real clinical workflows.
paper_title: Heterogeneity-Adaptive Diffusion Schrodinger Bridge for PET-Guided Whole-Body MRI Translation
